spec: Given a departure hour and minute (0-23, 0-59) and a non-negative flight duration in minutes, return how many midnights are crossed before arrival, as a non-negative integer day count (0 if arrival happens the same calendar day).

Given a time of day as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59) and an integer offset in minutes, return "previous" if applying the offset moves the date to an earlier day, "next" if it moves to a later day, or "same" if the date is unchanged.

Given a start and end integer day number (start <= end), where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively (so day_number % 7 gives the weekday, 5=Saturday, 6=Sunday), return the count of weekend days (Saturday or Sunday) in the inclusive range [start, end].

Given a start and end integer day number (start <= end), where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively (so day_number % 7 gives the weekday, 5=Saturday, 6=Sunday), return the count of weekdays (Monday through Friday) in the inclusive range [start, end].

Given a start and end integer day number (start <= end) and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively, return the count of days in the inclusive range [start, end] that fall on that weekday.

Given an integer day number, where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively (day_number % 7 gives the weekday, 5=Saturday, 6=Sunday), return the smallest day number that is greater than or equal to the given one and falls on a weekend.

Given an integer day number, where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively (day_number % 7 gives the weekday, 5=Saturday, 6=Sunday), return the smallest day number that is greater than or equal to the given one and falls on a weekday (Monday-Friday).

Given a start and end integer day number (start <= end), where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively, return the number of complete Saturday-then-Sunday pairs that fall entirely within the inclusive range [start, end].
Given a starting weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) and an integer number of days to advance n (which may be negative or larger than a week), return the resulting weekday number (0-6).

Given an integer day number and a positive integer n, where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively, return the day number of the n-th weekend day at or after the given day number (n=1 means the first weekend day found, counting the given day itself if it is a weekend).
Given an integer day number, where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively, return True if that day falls on a Saturday or Sunday, and False otherwise.

Given a start and end integer day number (start <= end), where day number 0 represents a Monday and day numbers increase consecutively, and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) that are treated as non-business days, return the count of business days in the inclusive range [start, end].

Given a starting integer day number, a non-negative integer n, and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) treated as non-business days, return the day number reached after moving forward n business days from the starting day (the starting day itself is not counted).
Given an integer day number and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) treated as non-business days, return the largest day number strictly less than the given one that is a business day.

Given an integer day number and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) treated as non-business days, return the day number itself if it is already a business day, otherwise the smallest larger day number that is a business day.

Given a start and end integer day number (start <= end) and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) treated as non-business days, return the count of non-business days in the inclusive range [start, end].

Given a starting integer day number, a target integer day number (target >= start), and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) treated as non-business days, return the number of business days in the range strictly after start up to and including target.

Given a week's starting integer day number (a 7-day window [week_start, week_start+6]) and a tuple of weekday numbers (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) treated as non-business days, return the largest day number in that window that is a business day. The window is guaranteed to contain at least one business day.

Given a non-negative integer number of total seconds, return a string "Hh MMm SSs" giving whole hours (no leading zero), remaining minutes (always two digits) and remaining seconds (always two digits).
Given a non-negative integer number of total hours, return a string "Dd HHh" giving whole days (no leading zero) and remaining hours (always two digits).

Given a non-negative integer number of total minutes, return a human-readable string: if there are whole hours, include "N hour" or "N hours"; if there are remaining minutes, or the total is zero, also include "N minute" or "N minutes"; the parts are joined with a single space, and units of exactly 1 use the singular form.
Given a non-negative integer number of total minutes, return a string "H:MM": whole hours with no leading zero, followed by a colon and remaining minutes always shown as two digits.
Parse a duration string of the form "Xh YYm" (hours with no leading zero, then minutes always two digits) and return the total number of minutes it represents as an integer.

Parse a human-readable duration string composed of one or two parts separated by a single space, each part an integer followed by "hour"/"hours" or "minute"/"minutes" (e.g. "2 hours 5 minutes", "1 hour", or "0 minutes"), and return the total number of minutes it represents.

Given a (possibly negative) integer number of total seconds, return a signed clock string: the absolute value formatted as "HH:MM:SS" (each field zero-padded to two digits, hours may exceed two digits), preceded by "-" if the input was negative.

Given a non-negative integer number of total minutes, return a string "Dd HHh MMm" giving whole days (no leading zero), remaining hours (always two digits) and remaining minutes (always two digits), always showing all three parts even if zero.

Given the current time and a target time, each a string "HH:MM", return the number of whole minutes until the target time occurs next: 0 if they are equal, otherwise the minutes remaining today, or if the target has already passed today, the minutes until it occurs tomorrow.

Given a start time and end time, each a string "HH:MM:SS", return the number of whole seconds from start to end. If the end time is less than or equal to the start time, assume the interval crosses midnight into the next day.

Given a start time and end time, each a string "HH:MM", return the clock time "HH:MM" exactly halfway between them (rounding down to the nearest minute). If the end time is earlier than the start time, assume the interval crosses midnight into the next day.

Given the current time as a string "HH:MM" and a list of one or more target time strings "HH:MM", return the smallest number of whole minutes until any of the targets occurs (using the rule that a target equal to the current time is 0 minutes away, and a target earlier than the current time occurs tomorrow).

Given a start time and end time, each a string "HH:MM", return the elapsed duration formatted as "Hh MMm" (hours with no leading zero, minutes always two digits). If the end time is less than or equal to the start time, assume the interval crosses midnight into the next day.

Given the current time and an alarm time, each a string "HH:MM", and a boolean already_rang_today indicating whether the alarm has already gone off once today, return the number of whole minutes until the alarm next rings. If already_rang_today is True, the next ring is always tomorrow at the alarm time; otherwise use the usual rule (0 if equal to current time, wrap to tomorrow if the alarm time has already passed).

Given a date as (year, month, day) integers and an integer n (which may be negative), return the (year, month, day) tuple of the date n days later, correctly handling month and year boundaries and leap years.

Given a date string "YYYY-MM-DD" and an integer n (which may be negative), return the ISO date string "YYYY-MM-DD" of the date n days later, correctly handling month and year boundaries and leap years.

Given a date as (year, month, day) integers and an integer number of weeks n (which may be negative), return the (year, month, day) tuple of the date n*7 days later, correctly handling month and year boundaries and leap years.

Given a date as (year, month, day) integers and an integer number of months n (which may be negative), return the (year, month, day) tuple after adding n months to the month/year, clamping the day to the last valid day of the resulting month if necessary (e.g. adding 1 month to January 31 gives February 28 or 29).

Given a date as (year, month, day) integers and an integer number of months n (which may be negative), return the (year, month, day) tuple after subtracting n months from the month/year, clamping the day to the last valid day of the resulting month if necessary.
Given a date as (year, month, day) integers, return the number of days remaining in that calendar year after the given date (0 if the date is December 31st), accounting for leap years.
Given a year and a non-negative integer n, return the (month, day) tuple of the date that is n days before December 31st of that year (n=0 means December 31st itself), accounting for leap years.
